title: Peace shows up in speech and gait
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 31
summary: The shabad opens by exposing ritual performed from self-will as the misery of an unwanted bride. It directs the heart toward saintly company and one-pointed Naam, then shows the fruit plainly: sweet speech, humble walking, and peace within.
whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose devotional language still outruns their conduct. Kept close, it lets peace become visible in tone, pace, and the body's way of moving through the world.
takeaway: Let this stay with you: when remembrance is real, it reaches the mouth and the walk.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਨਮੁਖ ਕਰਮ ਕਮਾਵਣੇ ਜਿਉ ਦੋਹਾਗਣਿ ਤਨਿ ਸੀਗਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: manmukh karam kamaavane jiau dhohaagan tan seegaar ||
lines.translation: The self-willed manmukh performs religious rituals, like the unwanted bride decorating her body.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੇਜੈ ਕੰਤੁ ਨ ਆਵਈ ਨਿਤ ਨਿਤ ਹੋਇ ਖੁਆਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: sejai ka(n)t na aaviee nit nit hoi khuaar ||
lines.translation: Her Husband Lord does not come to her bed; day after day, she grows more and more miserable.

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਿਰ ਕਾ ਮਹਲੁ ਨ ਪਾਵਈ ਨਾ ਦੀਸੈ ਘਰੁ ਬਾਰੁ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: pir kaa mahal na paaviee naa dheesai ghar baar ||1||
lines.translation: She does not attain the Mansion of His Presence; she does not find the door to His House. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਾਈ ਰੇ ਇਕ ਮਨਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhaiee re ik man naam dhiaai ||
lines.translation: O Siblings of Destiny, meditate on the Naam with one-pointed mind.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੰਤਾ ਸੰਗਤਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਰਹੈ ਜਪਿ ਰਾਮ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: sa(n)taa sa(n)gat mil rahai jap raam naam sukh pai ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Remain united with the Society of the Saints; chant the Name of the Lord, and find peace. ||1||Pause||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਸਦਾ ਸੋਹਾਗਣੀ ਪਿਰੁ ਰਾਖਿਆ ਉਰ ਧਾਰਿ ॥
lines.transliteration: gurmukh sadhaa sohaaganee pir raakhiaa ur dhaar ||
lines.translation: The Gurmukh is the happy and pure soul-bride forever. She keeps her Husband Lord enshrined within her heart.

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਿਠਾ ਬੋਲਹਿ ਨਿਵਿ ਚਲਹਿ ਸੇਜੈ ਰਵੈ ਭਤਾਰੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: miThaa boleh niv chaleh sejai ravai bhataar ||
lines.translation: Her speech is sweet, and her way of life is humble. She enjoys the Bed of her Husband Lord.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋਭਾਵੰਤੀ ਸੋਹਾਗਣੀ ਜਿਨ ਗੁਰ ਕਾ ਹੇਤੁ ਅਪਾਰੁ ॥੨॥
lines.transliteration: sobhaava(n)tee sohaaganee jin gur kaa het apaar ||2||
lines.translation: The happy and pure soul-bride is noble; she has infinite love for the Guru. ||2||

lines.gurmukhi: ਪੂਰੈ ਭਾਗਿ ਸਤਗੁਰੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਜਾ ਭਾਗੈ ਕਾ ਉਦਉ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: poorai bhaag satagur milai jaa bhaagai kaa udhau hoi ||
lines.translation: By perfect good fortune, one meets the True Guru, when one's destiny is awakened.

lines.gurmukhi: ਅੰਤਰਹੁ ਦੁਖੁ ਭ੍ਰਮੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਹੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: a(n)tarahu dhukh bhram kaTeeaai sukh paraapat hoi ||
lines.translation: Suffering and doubt are cut out from within, and peace is obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਭਾਣੈ ਜੋ ਚਲੈ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਪਾਵੈ ਕੋਇ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: gur kai bhaanai jo chalai dhukh na paavai koi ||3||
lines.translation: One who walks in harmony with the Guru's Will shall not suffer in pain. ||3||

lines.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਭਾਣੇ ਵਿਚਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹੈ ਸਹਜੇ ਪਾਵੈ ਕੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: gur ke bhaane vich a(n)mrit hai sahaje paavai koi ||
lines.translation: The Amrit, the Ambrosial Nectar, is in the Guru's Will. With intuitive ease, it is obtained.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਿਨਾ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਤਿਨ ਪੀਆ ਹਉਮੈ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਖੋਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: jinaa paraapat tin peeaa haumai vichahu khoi ||
lines.translation: Those who are destined to have it, drink it in; their egotism is eradicated from within.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਸਚਿ ਮਿਲਾਵਾ ਹੋਇ ॥੪॥੧੩॥੪੬॥
lines.transliteration: naanak gurmukh naam dhiaaieeaai sach milaavaa hoi ||4||13||46||
lines.translation: O Nanak, the Gurmukh meditates on the Naam, and is united with the True Lord. ||4||13||46||

structure: First, it begins by exposing performative religiosity as intimate misery rather than holiness.
Then, it roots peace in saintly company, one-pointed Naam, and love for the Guru.
Finally, it ends with the Guru's Will as ambrosia and egotism dying where peace becomes embodied.
